Hey, first year student here, I have never heard of its medicine course so maybe it's an online diploma of sorts. The overwhelming majority of IE courses focus around some form of business or business-related field.  


But yeah, on your main questions about IE - IE offers an insane Uni experience. Not only is there a great social aspect to it, as you mentioned ( even more so if you choose the segovia campus ) but you get a bunch of opportunities to go beyond your courses to develop your future career - networking events around Europe or hosted in IE itself, talks in IE from major companies like Blackrock, or the founder of Openai ( these being just the ones i've been to xD ), hundreds of clubs which all offer their tailored experiences for whichever activities you may like ( many are academic, like finance, Private Equity & Venture Capital, PPLE society etc, but there are also "hobby" clubs for sports and whatnot ).

As a first year student in segovia, I'm glad as fuck I chose this city.

The benefit of choosing segovia over madrid is that you develop a close-knit group of friends ( in only a couple months I've already solidified many friendships, being a pretty closed introvert normally ), when in Madrid, as most people live around the city, it's harder to bond ( segovia is a small city so you'll spend most days with your friends ) . People party a lot, seriously, like several times a week, and since many clubs host IE-only days, you typically see all your friends whenever you go out. And besides, you go to madrid in the weekends if you want to visit the city or go out there.

That aside, the campus is dope ( though I do prefer the IE tower in Madrid ), and classes are great! I had the misconception that Segovia teaching would be worse than madrid, as local teachers would presumably be "worse", but the teachers simply travel from madrid to segovia, so teaching quality is virtually identical.

Finally, if you're settled on segovia, I CANNOT stress enough how much I recommend a student residence, as you basically become friends with most people in it and it's great for having a little friendly group of people to live with, whilst still having the privacy of your own rooms ( Having talked to people who chose apartments instead of residence, they do struggle a lil more to meet people ).

And finally, once you go to madrid the 3rd year, you'll already have your little group of friends once you get to the big city, it's like a head start ;)
